Devereux Foundation (Devereux Advanced Behavioral Health), a multistate nonprofit behavioral healthcare organization headquartered in Villanova, PA, detected suspicious network activity on 2025-11-09 and determined that an unauthorized external actor had accessed certain systems 2025-11-06 through 2025-11-09. On 2025-11-28 a ransomware/extortion group calling itself "The Gentlemen" posted a dark-web leak-site claim threatening to publish stolen data within 9-10 days unless the victim made contact (per threat-intel trackers hookphish.com and dexpose.io). No source found confirms actual ransomware encryption or operational disruption at Devereux -- the victim's own breach notice and law-firm summaries (classaction.org, claimdepot.com) describe only unauthorized network access and data exposure, not encryption/outage. Per the 'never speculate' rule this is coded as action.hacking (Unknown variety/vector, since the entry technique is undisclosed) plus action.social/Extortion for the leak-site ransom demand, rather than action.malware/Ransomware -- consistent with the issue's own 'Hacking-ext-unknown' template tag rather than a Malware-ext-Ransomware template. Investigation concluded 2026-06-23 that exposed data included names, dates of birth, SSNs, driver's license/state ID numbers, US alien registration numbers, taxpayer ID numbers, digital/electronic signatures, financial account information, payment card data, and medical/health-insurance information, for current/former employees, clients (patients), donors, payors, and business partners. Reported to HHS 2026-01-08; to the Vermont AG 2026-07-23. victim.employee_count ('1001 to 10000') is approximated from a public web search on Devereux's total headcount (~6,500 employees across programs; sourced from company-profile aggregators, not the breach notices themselves). Actor attribution to 'The Gentlemen' (coded actor.external.variety Organized crime / motive Financial) comes from third-party ransomware-tracking sites, not from Devereux's own notice (which names no attacker) -- flagged as attacker/threat-intel-sourced rather than victim-confirmed, per the trust-attacker-claimed-details convention. discovery_method.internal.variety 'Infrastructure monitoring' is an inference from the notice's 'detected suspicious network activity' language; the specific monitoring tool/control is not stated. attribute.confidentiality.state left at the default 'Stored' since no source states the encryption status of the data at rest. data_total intentionally omitted: sources report inconsistent/partial per-state individual counts (e.g. a claimed 501 total alongside separate state breakdowns such as 5,341 in TX and 3,316 in MA that do not sum consistently) with no reliable aggregate. asset.assets and asset.cloud coded Unknown -- no source specifies which system types or hosting environment were affected. Ignored the 'PHIDBR2019' issue label per standing guidance (it is a noise/artifact tag, not a data signal, and its embedded year is not the incident year). credit_monitoring/years reflect Devereux's offer of 24 months of Experian IdentityWorks coverage per claimdepot.com.

event_chain.summary: Extortion for payment via leak-site threat

summary: Devereux Foundation, a multistate behavioral healthcare nonprofit, detected an unauthorized external actor accessing its network Nov 6-9, 2025. The ransomware/extortion group 'The Gentlemen' later claimed the breach on a dark-web leak site, threatening to publish stolen data. Investigation confirmed exposure of names, SSNs, driver's license/ID numbers, financial account and payment card data, and medical/health-insurance information for employees, clients, donors, payors, and business partners.
